questions.question: In shared-memory multiprocessor architectures with cache coherence protocols, what does the term 'false sharing' refer to?
options: Multiple processors updating distinct, independent variables that reside within the same cache line, causing unnecessary coherence invalidations.
A hardware security flaw where speculative execution leaks cache tags across isolated memory enclaves.
Two processing cores simultaneously contending for the exact same spinlock variable in main memory.
The physical time-multiplexing of functional units between threads in a simultaneous multithreading (SMT) pipeline.
An erroneous protocol state where two independent caches simultaneously believe they hold exclusive modified ownership of a block.

questions.question: In deep sub-micron ASIC physical design, how does cross-coupling capacitance between adjacent parallel interconnects primarily affect signal timing when both wires switch simultaneously in opposite directions?
options: It cancels out the net mutual capacitance entirely, reducing interconnect propagation delay to minimum values.
It increases the effective capacitance due to the Miller effect, resulting in increased propagation delay and degraded signal transition times.
It induces large DC currents directly into the bulk silicon substrate, leading to localized thermal runaway.
It permanently shifts the input switching thresholds of receiver standard cells toward ground.
It causes the clock distribution buffers on nearby nets to randomly flip logic polarities.

questions.question: In digital IC design, what is the primary purpose of inserting scan chains during the Design for Testability (DFT) process?
options: To dynamically modulate internal supply voltages during runtime operation to reduce active power consumption.
To protect input/output pads from electrostatic discharge (ESD) events during post-packaging test sequences.
To convert internal flip-flops into shift registers during test mode, making internal sequential states controllable and observable from external pins.
To enable physical non-invasive micro-probing of deep sub-micron wires using focused ion beams.
To automatically detect and reroute spare silicon tracks around fabrication defects in standard cell rows.

questions.question: In Static Timing Analysis (STA), what is a 'false path' and why is it explicitly specified as a timing exception?
options: A signal path that violates hold constraints due to excessive clock skew and must be lengthened with delay buffers.
A clock network branch exhibiting substantial duty-cycle distortion that must be ignored during setup timing runs.
A circuit path spanning two asynchronous clock domains that has already been verified via analog Spice simulations.
A topological path in the netlist that cannot be logically sensitized or activated under real functional operating conditions, preventing wasteful optimization.
A broken routing trace that results in an open circuit, flagged for manual Engineering Change Order (ECO) rerouting.

questions.question: In computer microarchitecture, what is the primary role of the Common Data Bus (CDB) in Tomasulo's dynamic instruction scheduling algorithm?
options: To serialize instruction decoding and dispatch to prevent out-of-order reorder buffer overflow.
To manage low-latency Direct Memory Access (DMA) transfers between cache levels and physical memory.
To broadcast branch prediction recovery metadata directly to instruction fetch units.
To dynamically assign physical register identifiers from an architectural free list.
To broadcast execution results along with source tags simultaneously to all waiting reservation stations and register files, bypassing register file write latency.
